newsitem.title: INDIA: No change expected for HK's ethnic Indians - Delhi.
newsitem.headline: No change expected for HK's ethnic Indians - Delhi.

text.p: India said on Thursday it expected business as usual for ethnic Indians living in Hong Kong after the British colony is handed back to China.
"We have no information that there is going to be any change in their position," a Foreign Ministry spokesman told a news conference.
Newspapers have said rich ethnic Indians, fearing export curbs on gold and gems by Hong Kong's future administration, have been packing their jewellery and taking it to Singapore.
Hong Kong, home to some 28,000 people of Indian origin, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, ending more than 150 years of British rule.

Thousands of Hong Kong-based people of Indian origin hold British travel documents. Britain agreed in February to grant ethnic minorities passports before the handover to save them from being stateless.
The ministry spokesman said India, which won independence from Britain 50 years ago, hoped that trade with Hong Kong would not suffer after the handover.

Trade between India and Hong Kong totalled $2.7 billion in 1996. But more than 60 percent of India's exports to the territory were headed for China and about 40 percent of its imports from Hong Kong originated on the mainland.
India's trade with China, worth some $1.4 billion in 1996, was expected to swell to between $7 billion and $10 billion by 2005, the spokesman said.
